set.subject: reasoning
set.title: Box puzzle
set.stimulus:
Eight boxes — S, T, U, V, W, X, Y and Z — are kept one above another in a single stack, but not necessarily in the same order. The bottommost position is numbered 1 and the topmost position is numbered 8. Each box contains a different item — Caps, Watches, Shoes, Cups, Pens, Candles, Toys and Lamps.

1. More than four boxes are kept below the box containing Toys.
2. Only four boxes are kept below the box containing Pens.
3. As many boxes are kept below box S as above box Z.
4. Box W is kept at the top.
5. Only two boxes are kept between box X and box Z.
6. More than five boxes are kept below the box containing Watches.
7. Only one box is kept between the box containing Lamps and the box containing Shoes, and the box containing Shoes is kept below the box containing Lamps.
8. Box T is not kept immediately below box Z.
9. More than one box is kept between box X and the box containing Caps.
10. Only four boxes are kept between box Y and the box containing Candles.
11. The box containing Candles is kept above the box containing Toys.
12. Box U contains Candles.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Which box is kept fourth from the bottom?

steps: Start with the clues that fix a position outright: box W at position 8 (clue 4); the box containing Pens at position 5 (clue 2).
Now the box containing Toys can be at position 6, position 7 or position 8 (clue 1) — make 3 cases.
Case the box containing Toys at position 7: clue 12 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case the box containing Toys at position 8: clue 11 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case the box containing Toys at position 6 survives.
Now the box containing Watches can be at position 7 or position 8 (clue 6) — make 2 cases.
Case the box containing Watches at position 7: clue 12 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case the box containing Watches at position 8 survives.
The box containing Candles takes the only place left: position 7; Clue 10 → box Y at position 2.
Clue 12 → box U at position 7.
Now box S can be at position 1, position 3, position 4, position 5 or position 6 — make 5 cases.
Case box S at position 1: clue 3 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case box S at position 3: clue 9 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case box S at position 4: clue 5 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case box S at position 6: no place is left for box X — rejected.
Case box S at position 5 survives.
Clue 3 → box Z at position 4; Clue 5 → box X at position 1.
Clue 9 → the box containing Caps at position 4; Box T takes the only place left: position 6.
The same clues then place box V (position 3).
Now the box containing Shoes can be at position 1, position 2 or position 3 — make 3 cases.
Case the box containing Shoes at position 2: clue 7 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case the box containing Shoes at position 3: clue 7 cannot be satisfied — rejected.
Case the box containing Shoes at position 1 survives.
Continuing the same way, the remaining clues fix everyone.
Final arrangement (top to bottom): W, U, T, S, Z, V, Y, X.
From the final arrangement, position 4 → **Z**.
solution.shortcut: Start with clues 2, 4 — they fix a position outright — then work outwards through the clues that mention whoever is already placed.
solution.trap: **V** would be at position 4 only if clue 4 were ignored — clue 4 rules that arrangement out.
